headline: The Hockey Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a hockey system and have players teach it back, explain a delay or lineup change to officials and management, give feedback and settle conflicts, stop play and talk through an incident without blame, and write the game report in Spanish.

lessons.title: Teach the Neutral-Zone Trap to a Newly Traded Player
lessons.objective: Explain step by step how the team's neutral-zone trap works and why, then have the new player explain it back.

words.note: Common loanword on Spanish-speaking benches; verb: hacer forecheck.
Used for the gap between a defender and the attacker: mantener la distancia.
Mexico and US; in Spain la pizarra.
Latin American sports usage for a player trade.

words.en: First, the first forechecker pushes the puck toward the boards.
words.es: Primero, el primer delantero empuja el disco hacia la banda.

words.en: Then the wingers close the outside lanes.
words.es: Luego, los alas cierran los carriles laterales.

words.en: We don't press high because we want them to make the mistake.
words.es: No presionamos alto porque queremos que ellos cometan el error.

words.en: That's why you don't chase the attacker; you close your lane.
words.es: Por eso tú no persigues al atacante; cierras tu carril.
words.note: Informal tú, coach to player.

words.en: On your old team they attacked; here we wait.
words.es: En tu equipo anterior atacaban; aquí esperamos.

words.en: Okay, now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: A ver, explícamelo tú ahora, paso por paso.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Why do you think both defensemen don't step up?
words.es: ¿Por qué crees que no suben los dos defensas?

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Julián, a newly traded defenseman: explain the neutral-zone trap step by step with primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have him explain it back to you and correct what he mixes up.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero cerramos el carril central y luego esperamos el error.
examples.en: First we close the middle lane and then we wait for the mistake.

examples.es: Aquí no subes al forecheck; por eso mantienes la distancia en la línea azul.
examples.en: Here you don't jump into the forecheck; that's why you keep your gap at the blue line.

lessons.title: Why We Chip It Out Instead of Forcing the Pass
lessons.objective: Explain to a skeptical forward why and when the team chips the puck out instead of forcing a pass.

words.note: Spain; verb: regatear.
Sacarlo por el cristal = chip it off the glass.
Spain; in Latin America el celular.
Por el medio = through the middle.

words.en: If you force the pass through the middle, you lose it.
words.es: Si fuerzas el pase por el medio, lo pierdes.
words.note: Informal tú, coach to junior player.

words.en: When there's pressure, you chip it off the glass.
words.es: Cuando hay presión, se saca por el cristal.

words.en: With a one-goal lead, you don't take risks in your own zone.
words.es: Con ventaja mínima, no se arriesga en zona propia.

words.en: Okay, that dangle is beautiful, but how often does it work?
words.es: Vale, ese regate es precioso, pero ¿cuántas veces sale bien?
words.note: Vale is Spain's everyday okay.

words.en: In that clip the opponent isn't pressing, that's why it works.
words.es: En ese vídeo el rival no presiona, por eso funciona.

words.en: Your talent is used in the offensive zone, not here.
words.es: Tu talento se usa en la zona ofensiva, no aquí.

words.en: I'm not telling you not to dangle; I'm telling you when.
words.es: No te digo que no regatees; te digo cuándo.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Nicolás, a junior forward who loves to dangle: explain when and why the team chips the puck out, using impersonal se (se saca por el cristal) and si + present (si fuerzas el pase, lo pierdes), then have him explain the rule back.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se saca por la banda; si fuerzas el pase por el centro, lo pierdes)

examples.es: Se saca por el cristal cuando te presionan dos.
examples.en: You chip it off the glass when two players pressure you.

examples.es: Si fuerzas el pase por el medio, lo pierdes y nos marcan.
examples.en: If you force the pass through the middle, you lose it and they score on us.

lessons.title: Training a Call-Up Goalie on Rebound Control
lessons.objective: Give clear corrections to a young goalie on steering rebounds to the corner, then have him teach the drill back.

words.note: Loanword used on the bench and in the crease.
Many goalies simply say el blocker.
Mexico and US; cubeta = bucket.

words.en: Send it to the corner with the blocker.
words.es: Mándalo a la esquina con el bloqueador.
words.note: Informal tú, coach to young goalie.

words.en: Don't leave it in the slot, Iker.
words.es: No lo dejes en el slot, Iker.

words.en: If you can't steer it away, cover it.
Turn the pad and direct it outside.
words.es: Gira el protector y dirígelo hacia afuera.

words.en: Rocío, shoot low to his blocker side, please.
words.es: Rocío, tírale bajo, al lado del bloqueador, por favor.

words.en: Now you show me: how do you send it to the corner?
words.es: Ahora enséñamelo tú: ¿cómo lo mandas a la esquina?

words.en: Well done, that looks much better.
words.es: Bien hecho, así se ve mucho mejor.

lessons.speaking: You are the goalie coach, and the AI is Iker, a 17-year-old call-up goalie: correct his rebound control with commands like mándalo a la esquina, cúbrelo and no lo dejes en el slot, then have him teach the drill back to you.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (mándalo a la esquina, cúbrelo, no lo dejes en el slot)

examples.es: Mándalo a la esquina, no al centro.
examples.en: Send it to the corner, not to the middle.

examples.es: No lo dejes en el slot; cúbrelo con el guante.
examples.en: Don't leave it in the slot; cover it with your glove.

lessons.title: Walk the Staff Through the League Concussion Protocol
lessons.objective: Read the league's concussion protocol aloud and explain to staff what must happen before an athlete returns.

words.note: Alta is feminine but takes el: el alta, la firma del alta.
Mexico and US sports usage.

words.en: Read step number 3 of the protocol with me.
words.es: Lean conmigo el paso número 3 del protocolo.
words.note: Ustedes command to the staff.

words.en: Per the protocol, with any symptom the player doesn't return that day.
words.es: Según el protocolo, con cualquier síntoma el jugador no regresa ese día.

words.en: After each stage, we have to review the symptoms with the doctor.
words.es: Después de cada etapa, hay que revisar los síntomas con el médico.

words.en: Every symptom has to be written down on the league form.
words.es: Hay que anotar cada síntoma en el formulario de la liga.

words.en: Tomás, we don't do the quick check on the bench anymore.
words.es: Tomás, ya no hacemos la revisión rápida en la banca.
words.note: Informal, between coworkers.

words.en: We don't decide the return; the team doctor decides it.
words.es: Nosotros no decidimos el regreso; lo decide el médico del equipo.

words.en: Before signing anything, call the team doctor.
words.es: Antes de firmar nada, llamen al médico del equipo.

words.en: Elena, can you keep the log for each stage?
words.es: Elena, ¿usted puede llevar el registro de cada etapa?
words.note: Formal usted with a new colleague.

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI is Tomás, the equipment manager, with assistant Elena: read the league concussion protocol aloud and explain each step before a player returns, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que, citing the protocol and the team doctor.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de volver al hielo, hay que tener el alta del médico según el protocolo)

examples.es: Antes de volver al hielo, hay que tener el alta del médico, según el protocolo.
examples.en: Before returning to the ice, the player must have the doctor's clearance, per the protocol.

examples.es: Después de pasar una etapa sin síntomas, hay que esperar la revisión del médico.
examples.en: After completing a stage without symptoms, we have to wait for the doctor's review.

lessons.title: Soft Ice and Ruts Before Puck Drop: Propose a Delay
lessons.objective: Describe what happened to the ice during warm-up and propose a safe plan to the rink manager and the referee.

words.note: Common in Spain; many people also say la Zamboni.
Feminine for Pilar; a man is el responsable.
Feminine noun, but it takes el: el acta, las actas.

words.en: The ice was already soft when the resurfacer broke down.
words.es: El hielo ya estaba blando cuando se rompió la pulidora.

words.en: During warm-up, two players fell in front of the net.
words.es: Durante el calentamiento, dos jugadores se cayeron delante de la portería.

words.en: There are deep ruts right in front of the crease.
words.es: Hay surcos profundos justo delante del área de portería.

words.en: Could we delay the start until they fix the resurfacer?
words.es: ¿Podríamos retrasar el inicio hasta que arreglen la pulidora?
words.note: Formal and polite; good for the rink manager.

words.en: Mr. Molina, would you mind checking the ice with me?
words.es: Señor Molina, ¿le importaría revisar el hielo conmigo?
words.note: Formal (usted) for the referee.

words.en: How long would it take the technician to get here, Pilar?
words.es: ¿Cuánto tardaría el técnico en llegar, Pilar?

words.en: I wouldn't put the players on this ice.
words.es: Yo no pondría a los jugadores en este hielo.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is rink manager Pilar Escudero: describe what happened to the ice during warm-up with the preterite and imperfect (estaba blando cuando se rompió) and propose a delay with the conditional (podríamos retrasar el inicio).

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (el hielo estaba blando cuando se rompió la máquina; podríamos retrasar el inicio)

examples.es: El hielo estaba blando cuando se rompió la pulidora.
examples.en: The ice was soft when the resurfacer broke down.

examples.es: Podríamos retrasar el inicio media hora.
examples.en: We could delay the start half an hour.

lessons.title: Starting Goalie Out Sick: Dressing the Emergency Backup
lessons.objective: Compare the goalie options and announce tonight's new plan to the team and the emergency backup.

words.note: Spain usage; estar convocado = to be dressed for the game.
In Spain, a player's license to play in a league.

words.en: Daniel, you're going to start tonight.
words.es: Daniel, esta noche vas a empezar tú.
words.note: Informal (tú) between coach and player.

words.en: Hugo has a fever and will stay at the hotel.
words.es: Hugo tiene fiebre y se quedará en el hotel.

words.en: Óscar, you're going to dress as the emergency goalie.
words.es: Óscar, vas a estar convocado como portero de emergencia.

words.en: You have less experience than Daniel, but you're as calm as he is.
words.es: Tienes menos experiencia que Daniel, pero estás tan tranquilo como él.

words.en: Most likely you won't play, but you'll be ready.
words.es: Lo más probable es que no juegues, pero estarás preparado.

words.en: If Daniel gets hurt, you'll go in.
words.es: Si Daniel se lesiona, entrarás tú.

words.en: Guys, change of plans: Daniel will start tonight.
words.es: Chicos, cambio de planes: Daniel saldrá de titular esta noche.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Óscar Lima, the emergency goalie: tell him tonight's new plan with the future and ir a (va a empezar Daniel, estarás convocado) and compare the goalies with más/menos ... que and tan ... como.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (va a empezar Daniel; Óscar tiene menos experiencia que él, pero está tan tranquilo como...)

examples.es: Va a empezar Daniel; Hugo se quedará en el hotel.
examples.en: Daniel is going to start; Hugo will stay at the hotel.

examples.es: Óscar tiene menos experiencia que Daniel, pero está tan tranquilo como él.
examples.en: Óscar has less experience than Daniel, but he's as calm as he is.

lessons.title: Explain a Hit from Behind to the League Supervisor
lessons.objective: Narrate exactly what happened on a hit from behind, with times and jersey numbers, to the league's supervisor.

words.note: Feminine for Lucía; a man is el supervisor.
Spain usage; also el número.
Spain usage for the rink boards.
Spain usage; ala is also heard.
Feminine noun, but it takes el: el acta.

words.en: At 14:32, number 27 pushed him into the boards.
words.es: En el 14:32, el número 27 lo empujó contra la valla.

words.en: Bruno had his back turned and didn't see the player coming.
words.es: Bruno estaba de espaldas y no vio venir al jugador.

words.en: He hit the boards head-first and didn't move.
words.es: Chocó de cabeza contra la valla y no se movió.

words.en: The referee called a hit from behind and ejected number 27.
words.es: El árbitro señaló carga por detrás y expulsó al número 27.

words.en: The medics took him off on a stretcher at 20:15.
words.es: Los médicos lo sacaron en camilla a las 20:15.

words.en: That version isn't accurate; please review the video.
words.es: Esa versión no es correcta; revise el vídeo, por favor.
words.note: Formal (usted) for the supervisor.

words.en: I saw it all from the bench, straight on.
words.es: Yo lo vi todo desde el banquillo, de frente.
words.note: Banquillo is Spain usage for the bench.

words.en: I can send you the video of the play tonight.
words.es: Le puedo enviar el vídeo de la jugada esta noche.
words.note: Formal (le = to you, usted).

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is league supervisor Lucía Cordero: narrate the hit on Bruno Salas step by step in the preterite (lo empujó, cayó, lo sacaron), giving exact times and jersey numbers such as en el 14:32 and el número 27.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (en el 14:32 del segundo periodo, el número 27 lo empujó contra la valla)

examples.es: En el 14:32 del segundo periodo, el número 27 lo empujó contra la valla.
examples.en: At 14:32 of the second period, number 27 pushed him into the boards.

examples.es: Bruno cayó de cabeza y los médicos entraron en el 14:33.
examples.en: Bruno went in head-first and the medics came on at 14:33.

lessons.title: Saying No: The Owner Wants the Injured Captain to Play
lessons.objective: Refuse to dress a player who has no medical clearance and explain the reasons firmly to the owner.

words.note: El dueño is also common and less formal.
Spain usage: hay lleno = it's sold out.
Informal: dar el visto bueno = to give the OK.

words.en: I don't recommend that he play without the doctor's clearance.
words.es: No recomiendo que juegue sin el alta del médico.
words.note: No recomiendo que takes the subjunctive: juegue, not juega.

words.en: Mr. Bermejo, please don't ask me for that.
words.es: Señor Bermejo, no me pida eso, por favor.
words.note: Formal (usted) negative command for the owner.

words.en: Álex, don't put your gear on yet.
words.es: Álex, no te pongas el equipo todavía.
words.note: Informal (tú) for the captain.

words.en: Don't put him on the game sheet yet.
words.es: No lo apuntes en la hoja de partido todavía.
words.note: Informal (tú) to a staff member.

words.en: Even if you feel fine, the league protocol doesn't allow it.
words.es: Aunque te sientas bien, el protocolo de la liga no lo permite.

words.en: If he takes a second hit, he could lose his career.
words.es: Si recibe un segundo golpe, puede perder la carrera.

words.en: It's not my decision; it's a medical decision.
words.es: No es mi decisión; es una decisión médica.

words.en: I'd rather lose the derby than lose my captain.
words.es: Prefiero perder el derbi antes que perder a mi capitán.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is owner Ricardo Bermejo: refuse to dress captain Álex Navarro without medical clearance, using negative commands (no me pida eso, no lo pongas) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, firm but respectful.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo pongas en la lista; no recomiendo que juegue sin el alta)

examples.es: No lo pongas en la lista hasta que llegue el alta.
examples.en: Don't put him on the list until the clearance comes.

examples.es: No recomiendo que Álex juegue sin el alta del médico.
examples.en: I don't recommend that Álex play without the doctor's clearance.

lessons.title: Feedback for a Veteran Who Stopped Backchecking
lessons.objective: Give honest, respectful feedback to a veteran forward and state clearly what you want him to change.

words.note: Many players also say el backcheck.
Used with ponerse: no te pongas a la defensiva.

words.en: Raúl, I want you to come back on every shift.
words.es: Raúl, quiero que vuelvas atrás en cada turno.
words.note: Informal: coaches usually use tú with their players.

words.en: I recommend you watch these clips with me.
words.es: Te recomiendo que mires estos clips conmigo.

words.en: Look here: the opponent gets away alone and you stay up ice.
words.es: Mira aquí: el rival se va solo y tú te quedas arriba.

words.en: I'm not saying this to attack you; I'm saying it because I need you.
words.es: No te lo digo para atacarte; te lo digo porque te necesito.

words.en: I understand it bothers you, but the clips are clear.
words.es: Entiendo que te moleste, pero los clips son claros.
words.note: Entiendo que + subjunctive when reacting to a feeling.

words.en: I need the young players to see an example in you.
words.es: Necesito que los jóvenes vean en ti un ejemplo.

words.en: What do you need from me for this to change?
words.es: ¿Qué necesitas de mí para que esto cambie?

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Raúl Montero, a veteran forward, on the team bus after a loss: show him the clips on the tablet, give honest feedback, and say what must change with quiero que and te recomiendo que, staying respectful.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que vuelvas atrás; te recomiendo que mires el vídeo)

examples.es: Quiero que vuelvas atrás hasta nuestra zona.
examples.en: I want you to come back to our zone.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que mires el video esta noche.
examples.en: I recommend you watch the video tonight.

lessons.title: Two Defenders Clash Over a Penalty-Corner Goal
lessons.objective: Hear both sides of a locker-room argument, report what each said, and agree on a way forward.

words.note: Usual term in Spain; you will also hear penalti córner.

words.en: Carla, you first; Sofía, then it's your turn.
words.es: Carla, tú primero; Sofía, luego te toca a ti.

words.en: Carla says you weren't in your position at the near post.
words.es: Carla dice que no estabas en tu posición en el primer palo.

words.en: Sofía, did you think Carla was covering the near post?
words.es: Sofía, ¿tú pensabas que Carla cubría el primer palo?

words.en: So neither of you knew who was going out first.
words.es: Entonces ninguna de las dos sabía quién salía primero.

words.en: We're not looking for someone to blame; we're looking for a solution.
words.es: Aquí no buscamos culpables; buscamos una solución.

words.en: Shouting at each other in front of the team doesn't help anyone.
words.es: Gritaros delante del equipo no ayuda a nadie.
words.note: Spain: vosotros forms (gritaros, estáis) when speaking to both players.

words.en: Do you both agree with this division of roles?
Tomorrow we'll go over the set play with the whole team.
words.es: Mañana repasamos la jugada ensayada con todo el equipo.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI plays defenders Carla and Sofía in the physio room: hear both sides, report what each said with dijo que and pensaba que plus the imperfect, and agree on who covers which post at penalty corners.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (dijo que no estabas en tu posición; ella pensaba que tú cubrías el poste)

examples.es: Carla dijo que no estabas en tu posición.
examples.en: Carla said you weren't in your position.

examples.es: Sofía pensaba que tú cubrías el primer palo.
examples.en: Sofía thought you were covering the near post.

lessons.title: Keeping the Team Together Through a Six-Game Skid
lessons.objective: Lead a frank team meeting during a losing streak and make concrete commitments for the coming week.

words.en: Tomorrow we'll practice off-puck play at 10:00.
words.es: Mañana entrenaremos el juego sin disco a las 10:00.

words.en: We're going to turn this around together, keep your heads up.
words.es: Lo vamos a sacar adelante juntos, ánimo.

words.en: Mateo, thanks for saying it; we need that honesty.
words.es: Mateo, gracias por decirlo; necesitamos esa honestidad.

words.en: Gael, how do you see it? Your opinion counts here.
words.es: Gael, ¿tú cómo lo ves? Aquí tu opinión cuenta.
words.note: Informal: tú to a single player inside a team meeting.

words.en: This week each line will talk about one mistake and one solution.
words.es: Esta semana cada línea hablará de un error y una solución.

words.en: On Thursday we'll all have dinner together, no phones.
words.es: El jueves cenaremos todos juntos, sin celulares.

words.en: I'll be the first to own my mistakes.
words.es: Yo seré el primero en reconocer mis errores.

words.en: 6 losses don't erase what we've built.
words.es: 6 derrotas no borran lo que hemos construido.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is the team in a hotel conference room after a sixth straight loss: lead a frank meeting, hear captain Mateo and rookie Gael, and set concrete commitments with the future (entrenaremos, hablaremos) and ánimo.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana entrenaremos el juego sin disco; lo vamos a sacar adelante, ánimo)

examples.es: Mañana entrenaremos el juego sin disco.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll practice off-puck play.

examples.es: Cada línea verá su video antes del viernes.
examples.en: Each line will watch its video before Friday.

lessons.title: One Message, Four Listeners: Ref, GM, Rookie, Reporter
lessons.objective: Coach the new captain to switch between usted and tú for each listener, then have her practice it back.

words.note: Tutear means to address someone with tú.

words.en: Excuse me, Begoña, could you explain the decision on that play?
words.es: Disculpe, Begoña, ¿podría explicarme la decisión en esa jugada?
words.note: Formal: usted with the referee, even when you disagree.

words.en: Fernando, I'd like to talk to you about the play on the goal.
words.es: Fernando, quisiera hablar con usted sobre la jugada del gol.
words.note: Formal: quisiera softens a request to the GM.

words.en: Relax, it wasn't your fault; how about we watch it together?
words.es: Tranquila, no fue culpa tuya; ¿te parece si lo vemos juntas?
words.note: Informal: tú with a teammate.

words.en: We respect the referee's decision and we move on.
words.es: Respetamos la decisión de la árbitra y seguimos adelante.
words.note: Neutral statement for the press.

words.en: Inés, I'd rather not judge the refereeing right after the game.
words.es: Inés, prefiero no valorar el arbitraje en caliente.
words.note: En caliente means in the heat of the moment.

words.en: Valeria, always use usted with the referee, even when you're angry.
words.es: Valeria, con la árbitra siempre de usted, aunque estés enfadada.

words.en: Now you tell me, as if I were Fernando.
words.es: Ahora dímelo tú como si yo fuera Fernando.

words.en: How about we practice the 4 versions again?
words.es: ¿Te parece si practicamos las 4 versiones otra vez?

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is Valeria Gil, the new captain: show her how to talk about the disputed goal to the referee, the GM, a rookie and a reporter, switching usted and tú with quisiera, ¿podría...? and ¿te parece si...?, then have her practice it back.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿podría explicarme...?, ¿te parece si...?)

examples.es: Disculpe, ¿podría explicarme por qué se dio el gol?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you explain to me why the goal was allowed?

examples.es: ¿Te parece si vemos el vídeo juntas?
examples.en: How about we watch the video together?

lessons.title: Skate-Blade Cut in a Goalmouth Pileup: The Incident Report
lessons.objective: Narrate a skate-cut incident in time order and complete the league incident report in Spanish.

words.note: Spain: el parte is the standard word for an official report form.
Spain says la cuchilla; in Latin America you also hear la navaja.
Spain: the scramble of bodies in front of the net.
In speech, people usually just say los puntos.
Spain often shortens it to la fisio.

words.en: At 20:15, Marcos fell in the pileup.
words.es: A las 20:15, Marcos cayó en la melé.

words.en: Right after the whistle, I saw blood on the ice.
words.es: Justo después del silbato, vi sangre en el hielo.

words.en: While Noelia was applying direct pressure, I called the ambulance.
words.es: Mientras Noelia le hacía presión directa, yo llamé a la ambulancia.
words.note: Imperfect (hacía) for the ongoing action, preterite (llamé) for the completed one.

words.en: As soon as the bleeding stopped, we put a bandage on him.
words.es: En cuanto paró la hemorragia, le pusimos un vendaje.

words.en: Noelia, your notes say 20:18, but the clock showed 20:15.
words.es: Noelia, tus notas dicen 20:18, pero el reloj marcaba 20:15.
words.note: Informal: tú between coworkers.

words.en: Let's write down both times and explain the difference.
words.es: Pongamos las dos horas y expliquemos la diferencia.

words.en: Who else was in the pileup when he got cut?
words.es: ¿Quién más estaba en la melé cuando se cortó?

words.en: They took him to the hospital at 20:40 to get stitches.
words.es: Lo trasladaron al hospital a las 20:40 para ponerle puntos.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is athletic trainer Noelia Campos: narrate Marcos's skate-cut injury in time order for the league incident report, using a las 20:15, justo después de, mientras and en cuanto, and check each time against her notes.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las 20:15, justo después de, mientras, en cuanto)

examples.es: Justo después de la caída, Marcos se tocó la muñeca.
examples.en: Right after the fall, Marcos grabbed his wrist.

examples.es: Mientras los árbitros separaban a los jugadores, Noelia entró en el hielo.
examples.en: While the referees were separating the players, Noelia went onto the ice.

lessons.title: Near Miss in the Shooting Drill, Without Blame
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss in a shooting drill without blaming anyone and agree on a new drill rule.

words.note: Formal safety term; in conversation people say casi pasa algo.
Agrees with the person: agachado for a man.

words.en: It nearly hit Paula in the head.
words.es: Por poco le da a Paula en la cabeza.

words.en: Rubén, relax: nobody here is blaming you.
words.es: Rubén, tranquilo: aquí nadie te está culpando.
words.note: Informal: tú with a player.

words.en: It could have been serious, so let's talk about the system.
words.es: Podría haber sido grave, así que hablemos del sistema.

words.en: Paula, when you were bent down, could you see the shooters?
words.es: Paula, cuando estabas agachada, ¿veías a los tiradores?

words.en: If someone is picking up pucks, nobody shoots.
words.es: Si alguien recoge discos, nadie tira.

words.en: If nobody calls it out, the shooter can't know.
words.es: Si nadie avisa, el tirador no puede saberlo.

words.en: Starting tomorrow, we only shoot on my whistle.
words.es: A partir de mañana, solo se tira con mi silbato.

words.en: Something serious almost happened; thank you both for speaking up.
words.es: Casi pasa algo serio; gracias a los dos por contarlo.
words.note: Casi + present tense is the natural way to say almost happened.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI plays assistant Paula Serrano and shooter Rubén Castillo: talk through the near miss without blame, using casi, por poco and podría haber, and agree on a new drill rule with si clauses like si alguien recoge discos, nadie tira.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco le da en la cabeza; si alguien recoge discos, nadie tira)

examples.es: El disco casi le da en la cabeza; podría haberla lesionado.
examples.en: The puck almost hit her in the head; it could have injured her.

examples.es: Si alguien está detrás de la portería, nadie tira.
examples.en: If someone is behind the net, nobody shoots.

lessons.title: Lightning at the Pitch: Stop Play and Clear the Field
lessons.objective: Call a stop to play, give short commands to players and staff, and say what happens next if the storm continues.

words.note: Spain says el vestuario; Mexico often says el vestidor.

words.en: Everyone to the locker room, now!
Lorena, please stop the match: we can hear thunder.
words.es: Lorena, por favor, pare el partido: se oyen truenos.
words.note: Formal: usted command to the umpire.

words.en: Nobody stays under the trees or in the stands.
words.es: Nadie se queda bajo los árboles ni en las gradas.

words.en: According to the tournament protocol, we wait 30 minutes without thunder.
words.es: Según el protocolo del torneo, esperamos 30 minutos sin truenos.
words.note: Always name the protocol as the source of the waiting time.

words.en: If we hear another thunderclap, the waiting time will start over.
words.es: Si oímos otro trueno, el tiempo de espera empezará de cero.

words.en: If the storm continues, we won't go back on the pitch today.
words.es: Si la tormenta sigue, no volveremos al campo hoy.

words.en: Mr. Soler, I understand the schedule, but safety comes first.
words.es: Señor Soler, entiendo el horario, pero la seguridad es lo primero.
words.note: Formal: señor plus surname with the director.

words.en: Let's count the players: nobody can be missing.
words.es: Vamos a contar a los jugadores: que no falte nadie.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is umpire Lorena Vidal, then tournament director Javier Soler on the phone: stop play, clear the pitch with short commands like ¡todos al vestuario, ya!, and explain what comes next with si + present → future, citing the tournament's weather protocol.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si oímos otro trueno, nadie volverá al campo; ¡todos al vestuario, ya!)

examples.es: Si vuelve a tronar, avisaré a las familias por megafonía.
examples.en: If it thunders again, I'll alert the families over the PA.

examples.es: ¡Fuera del campo, todos, ya!
examples.en: Off the pitch, everyone, now!

lessons.title: Federation Auditor Reviews Our Youth Safeguarding Files
lessons.objective: Explain formally to an auditor how the club handles locker-room supervision, medical records and incident reports.

words.note: Spain: the official clearance required for anyone working with minors.
La delegada de protección if the officer is a woman.

words.en: In the locker rooms, two adults must always be present.
words.es: En los vestuarios siempre se exige la presencia de dos adultos.

words.en: Incident reports are filed under lock and key in this office.
words.es: Los informes de incidentes se archivan bajo llave en este despacho.

words.en: Medical records are only shared with authorized staff.
words.es: Los historiales médicos solo se comparten con el personal autorizado.

words.en: Ms. Aguirre, you are right: the date doesn't match.
words.es: Señora Aguirre, tiene usted razón: la fecha no coincide.
words.note: Formal: usted placed after the verb sounds extra polite.

words.en: We acknowledge the mistake, and I assure you it won't happen again.
words.es: Reconocemos el error y le aseguro que no se repetirá.

words.en: Pablo won't go back on the ice until his certificate is recorded.
words.es: Pablo no volverá a la pista hasta que se registre su certificado.

words.en: By what deadline should we send you the corrective action?
words.es: ¿En qué plazo debemos enviarle la medida correctora?
words.note: Formal: le refers to usted.

words.en: I'll send you a copy of the certificate tomorrow morning.
words.es: Le enviaré una copia del certificado mañana por la mañana.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is federation auditor Carmen Aguirre: explain formally, using usted and passive se (los vestuarios se supervisan, los informes se archivan bajo llave), how the club handles locker-room supervision, medical records and incident reports.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (los vestuarios se supervisan por dos adultos; los informes se archivan bajo llave)

examples.es: Los informes se archivan bajo llave y se revisan cada mes.
examples.en: Reports are filed under lock and key and reviewed every month.

examples.es: Antes de salir a la pista, se comprueba el certificado de cada entrenador.
examples.en: Before going on the ice, each coach's certificate is checked.

lessons.title: Write the Official Report on the Storm-Stopped Match
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal report on the suspended match with times, decisions taken, and the proposed replay.

words.note: Lorena is a woman: la árbitra.
An online post; colloquially also el post.
In formal reports: se adjunta como anexo.

words.en: I am sending you the official report on the suspended match.
words.es: Le remito el informe oficial sobre el partido suspendido.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: First, the match was stopped in minute 38.
words.es: En primer lugar, el partido se detuvo en el minuto 38.

words.en: Next, the umpire ordered the field and stands to be cleared.
words.es: A continuación, la árbitra ordenó el desalojo del campo y las gradas.

words.en: Due to the storm, the match could not resume that day.
words.es: Debido a la tormenta, el partido no pudo reanudarse ese día.

words.en: Therefore, we propose replaying the full match on 14 June.
words.es: Por lo tanto, proponemos repetir el partido completo el 14 de junio.

words.en: In conclusion, the tournament's weather protocol was followed.
words.es: En conclusión, se siguió el protocolo meteorológico del torneo.

words.en: I attach the umpire's notes with the exact times.
words.es: Adjunto las notas de la árbitra con las horas exactas.

words.en: Mrs. Costa, I invite you to read the official report.
words.es: Señora Costa, le invito a leer el informe oficial.
words.note: Formal, calm reply to a parent's public post.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is tournament director Javier Soler: read him your official report on the suspended match, ordering times and decisions with en primer lugar, a continuación, debido a and por lo tanto, and close by proposing the replay with en conclusión.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, a continuación, debido a, por lo tanto, en conclusión)

examples.es: Debido a los truenos, la árbitra detuvo el juego a las 17:42.
examples.en: Due to the thunder, the umpire stopped play at 17:42.

examples.es: Por lo tanto, solicitamos a la federación la repetición del partido.
examples.en: Therefore, we request a replay of the match from the federation.

lessons.title: Ice Time Cancelled: Texts and Calls to Move the Game
lessons.objective: Write clear texts and make polite calls to reschedule a game after the rink cancels your ice time.

words.note: In Spain el delegado handles a team's logistics and contacts.
Marisa is a woman: la designadora.
Used for an away team's travel to the game.
Common polite phrase: perdone las molestias.
Standard sign-off for texts and emails in Spain.

words.en: Good evening, Esteban, sorry to call you so late.
words.es: Buenas noches, Esteban, perdone que le llame tan tarde.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would Sunday afternoon work for you?
words.es: ¿Le vendría bien jugar el domingo por la tarde?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Could you confirm the new date before Monday?
words.es: ¿Podría confirmarme la nueva fecha antes del lunes?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Guys, there's no game on Saturday: the rink has a breakdown.
words.es: Chicos, el sábado no hay partido: la pista tiene una avería.
words.note: Informal, for the team group chat.

words.en: Hello, Marisa, I'm leaving you this message about Saturday's game.
words.es: Hola, Marisa, le dejo este mensaje por el partido del sábado.
words.note: Formal voicemail.

words.en: I'd appreciate it if you could call me back tomorrow.
words.es: Le agradecería que me devolviera la llamada mañana.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'll confirm the new time as soon as I have it.
words.es: Os confirmo la nueva hora en cuanto la tenga.
words.note: Informal, vosotros, to the team.

words.en: If that's all right with you, I'll send you a message with everything.
words.es: Si le parece bien, le mando un mensaje con todo.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is opposing manager Esteban Rey: explain that the rink cancelled Saturday's ice and agree on a new date using polite conditionals like ¿le vendría bien...? and ¿podría confirmarme...?, then read him the text you will send the team group.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿le vendría bien el domingo?, ¿podría confirmarme...?, un saludo)

examples.es: ¿Le vendría mejor el domingo a las 12:00?
examples.en: Would Sunday at 12:00 suit you better?

examples.es: ¿Podría confirmarme si hay árbitros para esa hora? Un saludo.
examples.en: Could you confirm whether there are referees for that time? Best regards.

lessons.title: Exit Meeting: A Contract Offer with Conditions
lessons.objective: Review a young forward's season and offer next season's role under clear conditions to him and his agent.

words.note: Verónica is a woman: la agente.
Llegar en forma = to arrive in shape.

words.en: Samuel, you've had a very good season: 18 goals and 22 assists.
words.es: Samuel, has hecho una temporada muy buena: 18 goles y 22 asistencias.
words.note: Informal, tú with the player.

words.en: We would give you more ice time as long as you improve on defense.
words.es: Te daríamos más minutos siempre que mejores en defensa.
words.note: Siempre que + subjunctive.

words.en: Ms. Paz, we cannot guarantee that spot in writing.
words.es: Señora Paz, no podemos garantizar ese puesto por escrito.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: We would review his role in December, based on his performance.
words.es: Revisaríamos su papel en diciembre, según su rendimiento.
words.note: Formal, to the agent.

words.en: Unless you get injured, you'll start on the second line.
words.es: A menos que te lesiones, empezarás en la segunda línea.
words.note: A menos que + subjunctive.

words.en: If the other club offers him more, we respect that.
words.es: Si el otro club le ofrece más, lo respetamos.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: What would Samuel need to sign this week?
words.es: ¿Qué necesitaría Samuel para firmar esta semana?
words.note: Formal, to the agent.

words.en: Your spot on the first unit depends on you.
words.es: Tu sitio en la primera unidad depende de ti.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the coach, and the AI is agent Verónica Paz with forward Samuel Robles: review Samuel's season and offer next year's role, setting conditions with the conditional and siempre que / a menos que plus the subjunctive, using tú with Samuel and usted with her.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (te ofreceríamos la segunda línea siempre que llegues en forma; a menos que...)

examples.es: Te ofreceríamos la segunda línea siempre que llegues en forma a la pretemporada.
examples.en: We would offer you the second line as long as you show up to preseason in shape.

examples.es: Firmaríamos hoy, a menos que usted prefiera esperar a la otra oferta.
examples.en: We would sign today, unless you prefer to wait for the other offer.

lessons.title: Capstone: Playoff Game Seven, From Morning Skate to Report
lessons.objective: Run a full playoff day in Spanish: teach, solve problems, lead people, handle an injury and write the report.

words.en: the call-up from the farm team

words.note: Spanish rinks usually call the protective glass el metacrilato.
Short for el fisioterapeuta; standard in Spanish team sports.

words.en: Leo, don't chase the puck: close your lane and wait.
words.es: Leo, no persigas el disco: cierra tu carril y espera.
words.note: Informal command to a player.

words.en: How long would it take to replace the broken glass?
words.es: ¿Cuánto tardarían en cambiar el metacrilato roto?
words.note: Polite conditional to arena staff.

words.en: We don't go on the ice until they check the new panel.
words.es: No salimos al hielo hasta que revisen el panel nuevo.

words.en: Not now: you'll talk it over in the locker room after the game.
words.es: Ahora no: lo habláis en el vestuario después del partido.
words.note: Informal, vosotros, to two players.

words.en: Nobody move Iván until the trainer arrives.
words.es: Que nadie mueva a Iván hasta que llegue el fisio.

words.en: I'm informing you that Iván will not play again tonight.
words.es: Le informo de que Iván no volverá a jugar esta noche.
words.note: Formal, to the league supervisor.

words.en: Due to the repair, the game started 25 minutes late.
words.es: Debido a la reparación, el partido empezó con 25 minutos de demora.
words.note: Written report register.

words.en: Whatever happens tonight, I'm proud of you.
words.es: Pase lo que pase esta noche, estoy orgulloso de vosotros.
words.note: Informal, to the whole team.

lessons.speaking: You are the head coach, and the AI plays Leo, arena staff, players, the trainer and the league supervisor: teach the trap with commands, ask about the glass repair with conditionals, calm the bench, get Iván help with the subjunctive and dictate the report with connectors.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar (connectors, commands, subjunctive, si clauses, formal and written register)

examples.es: En primer lugar, Iván recibió un disco en la cara a las 20:51; por lo tanto, no volvió a jugar.
examples.en: First, Iván took a puck to the face at 20:51; therefore, he did not return to play.

examples.es: Si el encargado no confirma la reparación, le pediremos al supervisor que retrase el inicio.
examples.en: If the maintenance supervisor doesn't confirm the repair, we'll ask the league supervisor to delay the start.
